root_causes.description: The checkout container was repeatedly killed and restarted during the incident window (Killing/Started/Created events with counts 2-3), matching the KubePodCrashLooping alert. CPU (~0.001 cores) and memory (~34MB) stayed normal, ruling out resource exhaustion; the 'definition changed, will be restarted' event indicates a container spec change/rollout triggered the crash loop, compounded by ImagePullBackOff on the pause image blocking sandbox creation.

evidence.query_or_id: Killing: Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted (count=2)
evidence.observed_value: checkout container killed and restarted; Created (count=3), Started (count=3), Pulled ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.0.0-checkout (count=3) during window
evidence.expected_baseline: no Killing/BackOff restart events for checkout pods

evidence.observed_value: BackOff pulling image gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest (count=3); Failed to pull: rpc error DeadlineExceeded (count=3)
evidence.expected_baseline: no image pull failures for pod sandbox images

evidence.observed_value: pod_restarts max=1.111, p95=1.111, mean=0.185 (anomaly flagged at 13:48:04-13:48:34)
evidence.expected_baseline: pod_restarts = 0; payment and frontend pods showed 0.000 across the same window

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage max=0.001 cores (near zero, pod down/restarting)
evidence.expected_baseline: normal checkout CPU baseline; rules out cpu_stress
normal working set, no OOM-level pressure; rules out memory_stress

root_causes.description: While the checkout pod was crash-looping, requests routed to it hung rather than failing fast: traces through checkout show p95 duration of ~54s (top traces at 15001-15002ms) with zero span errors, and checkout server error_rate stayed low (max 0.048). This is a secondary effect of the pod restarts, not an independent fault.

evidence.observed_value: user_get_recommendations trace, 15001ms, status ok; search_traces on checkout returned 20 traces, 0 errors, p95_duration=54483ms (also 2ef3350823423b78 and bd4dc69e977eba04 at 15002ms)
evidence.expected_baseline: p95 trace duration well under 1s for checkout-involved user journeys
error_rate < 0.01; errors stayed low because requests hung instead of aborting

evidence.observed_value: p99_latency_ms mean=4.850, max=4.850 (server-side spans fast; hang occurs upstream waiting on unavailable checkout)
evidence.expected_baseline: checkout p99 latency in single-digit ms is normal for served spans

root_causes.description: The frontend, which depends on checkout for order placement, showed an elevated server error rate (up to 0.105) during the window — upstream propagation of checkout unavailability, not an independent frontend fault (frontend pods had zero restarts).

evidence.observed_value: frontend error_rate mean=0.058, p95=0.100, max=0.105 during window

evidence.expected_baseline: 0 restarts — confirms errors originate from the checkout dependency
0 restarts — isolates the fault to checkout, not its downstream dependencies

remediation_steps: Inspect the checkout pod with kubectl describe pod -n otel-demo <checkout-pod> and kubectl logs --previous to capture the crash reason; the 'definition changed, will be restarted' event points to a spec/rollout change as the trigger.
If a recent deployment changed the checkout container spec, roll it back with kubectl rollout undo deployment/checkout -n otel-demo and verify the pod reaches Ready.

Resolve the ImagePullBackOff on gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest (pre-pull the image, fix registry access/timeout, or use a locally available pause image) so pod sandbox creation is not blocked during restarts.
Add readiness and startup probes on checkout so it is removed from endpoints while crash-looping, producing fast failures instead of 15-54s hung requests.
Add timeouts, retries with backoff, and a circuit breaker in frontend (and accounting/fraud-detection) calls to checkout to prevent cascading errors during checkout outages.
Alert on increases in kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total for checkout with a tighter threshold so crash loops are caught before user-facing impact.
